A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same D2SA research work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and included appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original U-Net and VarNet reconstruction experiments across four distribution shifts, adaptation timings, component ablations, and additional in-domain results in its appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains original reconstruction experiments and adds sampling-shift results, ZS-SSL comparisons, further ablations, and patient-level statistical analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 revise the stated MR-INR output shape from (B,1,H,W) to (B,2,H,W) and exempt transpose convolutions, as well as the final convolution, from freezing. The core two-stage framework remains intact. The explicit 1×1 projection added to the update equation was already described in v1.

E1.justification: V2 adds a random-to-uniform sampling-mask shift on fastMRI AXT2 brain data at fixed 4× acceleration. This introduces a distinct acquisition-pattern condition while retaining the same datasets, anatomical coverage, reconstruction task, and four original shift types.

E2.justification: V2 adds ZS-SSL to evaluated VarNet comparisons under both out-of-domain and in-domain conditions, with numerical results in Tables 4 and 6 and qualitative comparisons in Appendix F. The existing DIP-TTT, FINE, NR2N, and SSDU comparator families remain.

E3.justification: V2 introduces the fixed-4× sampling-shift protocol, a random-to-random mask control, and per-subject adjusted metrics defined as μ−0.5σ. Appendix A also revises the stated stopping criterion from increasing validation error to failure to decrease over monitored iterations. The original model sizes, cohort sizes, and training budgets remain; these descriptions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands component and stability analyses: Table 2 adds frozen-MR-INR and frozen-CNN/no-AD controls, Figure 6 compares directional and difference-convolution kernels, and Figure 8 examines patient-level performance distributions. These isolate component contributions and variability beyond v1's existing ablation and reconstruction examples.

E5.justification: V1 reports averages without formal variability or significance analysis. V2 adds a targeted analysis for two backbone/shift combinations using within-patient slice means and standard deviations, violin plots of adjusted scores, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with p<0.05 and p<0.01 annotations. Repeated-training-run counts or seed-based uncertainty are not introduced.

E6.justification: V2 adds sampling-shift, ZS-SSL, ablation, and statistical results. Retained entries also change: U-Net FINE+SST acceleration LPIPS changes from 0.689 to 0.389; in-domain 2× SSDU+MR-INR+SST changes from 0.838/29.20/0.218/49.7 to 0.901/30.25/0.192/44.2 for SSIM/PSNR/LPIPS/minutes (v1 Table 4; v2 Table 5). These are revised reported values, not established algorithmic improvements between versions.

T1.justification: V2 removes the extra term from the alpha derivative in v1 appendix Equation 45, yielding v2 Equation 41, while retaining the claimed optima and most derivations. Section 4.3 recasts the existing argument as a proposition and theorem. Appendix B also introduces the mathematical definition of the adjusted performance metric μ−0.5σ.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain patient-wise MR-INR adaptation, structural preservation through AD-based slice refinement, and improved reconstruction quality and adaptation efficiency. Updating validation from four to five shifts supplies additional evidence without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges the need for clinical undersampled-data validation and the limitation of independent 2D processing. Appendix D explains the retained AXT1PRE in-domain shortfall through an overly restrictive global prior. Section 4.3 newly qualifies the linear analysis as motivation for the nonlinear model, and the ablation discussion explains AD's usefulness with frozen CNNs.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents early-stopping windows of 30 for the SSL families and 100 for DIP-TTT, defines reported timing as combined stage durations, and specifies mask-generation relationships and seed controls. Most optimizer, architecture, loss-weight, hardware, and training-budget details were already supplied in v1's appendix.

R1.justification: V2 adds the ZS-SSL reference and an Appendix C discussion positioning D2SA's patient-level shared representations against independent-slice zero-shot reconstruction. The broader positioning relative to TTA, INRs, Functa, and existing reconstruction methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Related work, experimental descriptions, results discussion, and the conclusion receive extensive rewriting. The appendix is reorganized into sections A–F with a contents page, separate out-of-domain and baseline discussions, and visualizations grouped by backbone. These are substantial narrative and organizational changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 switches the main text to a single-column layout, redraws conceptual and AD diagrams, and adds performance-summary, kernel-ablation, and violin plots. Reconstruction panels gain ground-truth, zero-filling, and ZS-SSL displays. The U-Net out-of-domain table and VarNet qualitative example move into the appendix, while tables expand to accommodate sampling results.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens evaluation through the sampling-shift test, ZS-SSL comparisons, and more discriminating ablations, while improving reproducibility details and acknowledging concrete applicability limits. These provide useful gains around the retained core study. However, Figure 8 applies μ−0.5σ even to lower-is-better LPIPS, allowing greater variability to improve the adjusted score and weakening its stability interpretation. The overall improvement is therefore limited.
